relationship: Independent native runner screenshot lifecycle follows pinned policy, outcome, retry, pre-context-close, deduplication, PNG naming and attachment behavior. Native public-context observation replaces upstream browser instrumentation. A canonical weak public-browser registry discovers contexts created before worker setup; observation is installed before enumeration and deduplicates context identities. Disconnect and finalization remove registry entries. Private prepared/storage contexts are excluded.
limits: One five-second budget per capture batch, including recorder queue time; at most four captures run concurrently per scope.
At most 1024 attempted screenshots and 512 MiB retained image bytes per recording scope; overflows become explicit capture diagnostics.

Screenshot errors preserve the original outcome and retain up to 16 original error stacks, each bounded to 4096 characters, in one screenshot-error attachment with an additional-error count. Publish the complete body only after foreground cleanup because the pinned attachment push immediately sends reporter bytes. A stack-formatting failure falls back to the original data message.
Context-close temporary files are atomically captured, conditionally retained, then removed. Ordinary individual page close and direct browser close do not gain an extra capture hook.
exclusions: Trace and video policies remain explicitly unsupported.
Screenshot assertions, masks and broader page screenshot capabilities retain their existing boundaries.
Screenshot policy support alone does not establish original-config public-corpus completion.
